DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA comer Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 42 s. 2022 May 24, 2022 ATTY. ANGELA LENIN E. PAYCANA Vice Mayor Municipality of General Mariano Alvarez Province of Cavite Dear Vice Mayor Paycana: This has reference to your letter dated 15 March 2022 seeking legal opinion from this Department on the following queries: I. 2. 3. 4. 5. 6. Is the issuance and implementation of Administrative Order No. 2 proper, that assumes a reenacted budget, considering that the Annual Budget for 2022 has still on its deliberation process? If Administrative Order No. 2 is considered premature, does the operative fact doctrine apply? Are the enumerated items under MOOE considered "very essential" as contemplated in various DILG Legal Opinions? Can the Municipal Mayor solely and exclusively enumerate the list of "very essential" items or may the Sanggunian Bayan pass an ordinance enumerating the same? Is telephone allowance for the members of the Sanggunian Bayan members considered very essential? Are intelligence and confidential funds very essential items? And if these items can be disbursed without the approved annual appropriation ordinance from the Sanggunian Bayan or the budget is not ipso facto reenacted considering that even the POPS Plan for 2022 has been approved? Per your representation, the Municipal Mayor of GMA, Cavite, Hon. Maricel E. Torres issued Administrative Order No. 02 series of 20221 which authorized the disbursement of funds for the following essential operating expenses: a. b. c. d. e. f. g. Repair and Maintenance of Transportation Equipment; Repair and Maintenance of Buildings and Other Structure; Office Supplies Expense; Other Supplies and Material Expense; Rent Expense; Award and Reward Expense; Water Expense; Supplemental Administrative Order "Authorizing the Disbursement of 2021 Essential Operating Expenses Under the Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE), Salaries and Wages of all Existing Positions Including Statutory and Contractual Obligations of the Municipality 0 General Mariano Alvarez, Cavite Under the Reenacted Budget Pursuant to Section 323 of the Local Government Code of 1991 " "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

h. k. m. n. o. p. q. Also, Electricity Expense; Training Expense; Extraordinary and Miscellaneous Expense; Confidential Fund; Printing and Publication Expense; Drug and Medicine; Medical, Dental and Laboratory Supplies; Insurance Expense; Fidelity Bond; Assistance to Individuals in Crisis Situation you represented that the Subject Administrative Order was issued on an assumption that the Municipality is operating under a reenacted budget and you believe that the Administrative Order is invalid since its issuance is premised on a reenacted budget. Hence, the instant queries. With regard to the first and second queries, for failure of the Sangguniang Bayan to pass the budget ordinance for the current year, the Municipality of GMA is now on a reenacted budget following Section 323 of R.A. 7160 otherwise known as the Local Government Code of 1991 (LGC), viz: "Section 323. Failure to Enact the Annual Appropriations. - In case the sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beginning of the ensuing fiscal year, it shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until such ordinance is approved, and no other business may be taken up during such sessions. If the sanqqunian still fails to enact such ordinance after ninety (90) davs from the beqinninq of the fiscal year. the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the precedinq year shall be deemed reenacted and shall remain in force and effect until the ordinance authorizing the proposed appropriations is passed bv the sanqqunian concerned. However. only the annual appropriations for salaries and waqes of existing positions. statutory and contractual obliqations. and essential operatinq expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budqets for the preceding vear shall be deemed reenacted and disbursement of funds shall be in accordance therewith. In -the implementation of such reenacted ordinance, the local treasurer concerned shall exclude from the estimates of income for the preceding fiscal year those realized from nonrecurring sources, like national aids, proceeds from loans, sale of assets, prior year adjustments, and other analogous sources of income. No ordinance authorizing supplemental appropriations shall be passed in place of the annual appropriations. In case the revised income estimates be less than the aggregate reenacted appropriations, the local treasurer concerned shall accordingly advise the sanggünian concerned which shall, within ten (10) days from the receipt of such advice, make the necessary adjustments or reductions. The revised appropriations authorized by the sanggunian concerned shall then be the basis for disbursements." (Emphasizing and underlining supplied) From the foregoing, in case the Sanggunian concerned fails to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations at the beqinning of the ensuing fiscal year, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year shall be operationalized: Page 2 of 4

The Sanggunian shall continue to hold sessions, without additional remuneration for its members, until the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations is approved. If the Sanggunian still fails to enact such ordinance after the 90 days from the beqinninq of the fiscal year, the preceding year's budget shall remain in force and effect until such time that the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations is passed by the Sanggunian concerned.2 It is only upon the approval of the annual appropriations of the preceding that the same shall take effect. In the instant case, the ordinance authorizing the appropriations of the preceding year of GMA, Cavite shall be deemed reenacted for failure of the sanggunian bayan to pass the ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations for FY 2022 at the beginning of the ensuing year. Ergo, Administrative Order No. 02 series of 2022 issued by Mayor Torres is no longer necessary considering the term "deemed reenacted". The annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year was deemed reenacted in its entirety and will be valid and effective until an ordinance authorizing the annual appropriations is passed by the Sanggunian Bayan of GMA, Cavite. As to the third and fifth queries, we will answer them in one discussion since they are interrelated. Foremost, it is imperative to emphasize that a reenacted budget is as valid and effective as that of the previous year's budget. Hence, there is no need for such a determination of what are essential expenditures pertaining to MOOE in a reenacted budget because the MOOE in the previous year's budget is reenacted in its entirety.3 This Department has been very consistent on what should be included in the Maintenance and Other Operating Expenses (MOOE) and essential operating expenses, for your guidance may we cite DILG Legal Opinion No. 71 S. 20194, which states: "It is imperative to distinguish MOOE from essential operating expenses. MOOE is defined under the Glossary of Terms, Operations Manual for Local Government Units 2016 Edition, as an allocation to support the operations of local government units including those for supplies and materials. transportation and travel utilities and other maintenance activities. On the other hand, essential operating expenses refers to specific objects of expenditure under maintenance and other operating expenses. which are necessary for the operation of a particular local government unit to carry out its mandate in providing efficient and effective basic services. The Local Government Unif is in best position to identify expenses, which according to its best judgment, are essential to its operation." (Emphasis and underlining ours) As to the fourth query, please be informed that the issue of budget is not the sole responsibility of the municipal mayor. It is a principle on fiscal administration under the LGC that enactment of annual budget is a shared responsibility and complementary 2 DILG Legal Opinion NO. 72 s. 2021 3 DILG Legal Opinion No. 81 s. 2019, 14 November 2019 17 October 2019 Page 3 Of 4

function of both the local chief executive and the sanggunian.5 Although the local chief executive primarily determines what are the essential operating expenses, the Department has consistently opined that only "essential" (of the utmost importance; indispensable; extremely necessary) and not all operating expenses should be included in the MOOE.6 With regard to the sixth query. we invite your attention to the Budget Operations Manual for Local Government Units7 where it specifically states that the Confidential Expenses are part of the MOOE, viz: "The other costs, which are variable. are the Maintenance and Other Operatinq Expenses. These include Travel Expenses, Office Supplies Expenses, Rent, Water, Electricity, Fuel, Telephone Expenses, Internet Expenses, Security Services, Repair and Maintenance Expenses, Confidential Expenses, Printing Expenses, Extraordinary & Miscellaneous Expenses and Representation Expenses, etc." In line with this, we reiterate that the essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted. In case of reenacted budget, only the annual appropriations for essential operating expenses authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets for the preceding year shall be deemed reenacted.8 Hence, the Confidential Expenses can be disbursed without the approved annual appropriation ordinance provided that it was authorized in the annual and supplemental budgets as part of the essential operating expenses for the preceding year. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. Further, this opinion shall be without prejudice to any contrary opinion/s rendered by more competent authorities and the court. We hope to have addressed your concerns accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: GAN Underse tary for Local Government OUSLG/MLI/LLLS/LRALLD/I smi o/cp copy furnished: DIR.
